response.justification: The candidate is an experienced full-stack/web software developer (15+ years) with strong breadth across web, mobile, and some low-latency backend work, but there is essentially no overlap with the core requirements of this Principal Performance Architect role. There is no evidence of SoC or IP modeling, hardware-software co-design, GPU/accelerator architecture, SIMD/MIMD experience, or deep-learning workload optimization. The only adjacent items are brief C/C++ work at National Instruments and low-latency microservices in D, which are application-level rather than silicon architecture work. Education is a BS in Computer Science, which meets the formal bar (BS + 8 years), but the technical domain mismatch is decisive at principal level.
strengths: 15+ years of software engineering experience, meets BS+8yr bar
Low-latency, high-throughput systems work (D, async I/O, fibers)
Some systems/C/C++ exposure at National Instruments and embedded projects
concerns: No SoC/IP modeling or hardware architecture experience
No deep-learning, GPU, or AI accelerator workload optimization background
Career trajectory is web/full-stack, not principal-level silicon performance

key_factors.factor: Long general software engineering tenure and systems/low-latency exposure
